public_body: Southeastern Regional Planning And Economic Development District Board Of Commissioners
overall: Violation found: the Board entered executive session on Oct. 26, 2011 without required open-session procedures and without Purpose 1 notice and rights; no violation on denial of public comment; remedy was compliance and training.

allegations.summary: Board met in executive session on Oct. 26, 2011 without first convening in open session, stating a purpose, taking a roll-call vote, or stating whether it would reconvene.
allegations.key_passage: The Board was required to convene in open session before entering executive session, publicly state the purpose for the executive session, take a roll-call vote to enter the session, and state whether the Board would reconvene in open session following the executive session.

allegations.summary: Board discussed a former employee's dismissal in executive session without the 48-hour written notice and the rights required under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: by meeting in executive session to discuss the Ms. Lally's dismissal without providing her 48 hours' written notice and without affording her the rights guaranteed by executive session Purpose 1.

allegations.summary: Board voted in executive session on a personnel-policy review motion that was not a proper executive session topic; the complaint did not raise it.
allegations.key_passage: This vote was not appropriate for executive session, and should have occurred in open session.

allegations.summary: Complainant and her attorney were not allowed to address the Board at the Dec. 7, 2011 open session meeting after the vote.
allegations.key_passage: The Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by refusing to allow either Ms. Lally or her attorney to speak on her behalf during the Board's December 7, 2011 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant's additional claims that the Board violated personnel policy and stifled free speech fall outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We make no finding with respect to additional claims in Ms. Lally's January 19, 2011 letter that the Board's actions violated the SRPEDD's personnel policy or that the Board stifled her free speech, as those are not matters governed by the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent.
Attend an Open Meeting Law training within 60 days of receipt of the letter, approved by the AG (or view the AG training video), then send the AG a certification letter.
